chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the testimony of women in stoning, and he said: 'If there are three men and two women, it is valid; but if there are two men and four women, it is not valid in stoning.'
ai.seo_question: What is the valid combination of male and female witnesses for stoning in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific witness composition required for the hadd punishment of stoning (rجم), distinguishing it from general testimony rules. It establishes that a combination of three men and two women is valid, whereas a combination of two men and four women is not valid for this specific ruling. This distinction highlights the juristic nuance in Shia fiqh regarding the sufficiency of female witnesses when paired with varying numbers of male witnesses in capital cases.
